tips.title: Thinning Vallejo Model Air and Model Color for Airbrushing
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air requires a 1:1 ratio with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for optimal airbrushing consistency. For Model Color, mix at a 2:1 ratio (2 parts paint to 1 part thinner). Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint to prevent tip dry. Airbrush at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure for Model Air and 1.0-1.5 bar for Model Color. Test on a white plastic spoon; adjust ratio or pressure based on paint behavior.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Tamiya Acrylics
tips.text: For base coats, mix Tamiya Acrylics with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement at a 4:1 ratio (4 parts paint to 1 part cement). This creates a self-leveling, high adhesion mixture suitable for large, flat surfaces. Apply with a synthetic brush or by dipping the model into the mixture. Allow to dry for 24 hours before handling.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard Masks and Mr. Hobby Tape
tips.text: Apply Eduard Masks to define panel lines and edges before painting. Use Mr. Hobby Masking Tape for broader areas. Seal the model with a light coat of Mr. Hobby Super Clear (gloss) to prevent paint bleeding. Airbrush Vallejo Model Air or Model Color acrylics over the masked areas. Once dry, carefully remove masks and tape.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes for Realistic Weathering
tips.text: Shake AK Interactive Wash bottles well before use. Apply thin coats using a flat, synthetic brush or a dropper bottle, working from top to bottom and allowing washes to pool in panel lines and recesses. Remove excess with a damp, soft cloth or cotton swab. Allow to dry completely before handling. Neutralize dark washes with AK Interactive Decolor Wash (white spirit).

tips.title: Chipping Technique with a Sponge and Scale75 Chipping Medium
tips.text: Apply a coat of Scale75 Chipping Medium to the areas you want to chip, allowing it to dry for 10-15 minutes. Cut a small, flat piece of sponge and dip it in Vallejo Model Color, tapping off excess paint. Lightly dab the sponge onto the medium-coated areas, varying pressure for different chip sizes. Allow to dry for 30 minutes, then gently rub off the chipped paint with a soft cloth.
